context: The suite already carried a deterministic assertion on the case that broke production, that assertion is recorded as having failed, and the run still reported 9 of 9. Predicted baseline failure: the agent reads 'these cases lean on llm-rubric' as the defect, adds is-json to the four cases prompts/summarise.txt marks format=json, declares the suite repaired, and ships a configuration that would have reported green on the incident run all over again. eval/promptfooconfig.yaml sets defaultTest.threshold to 0.7 and eval/cases.jsonl weights every llm-rubric at 5 against 1 for the structural assertion, and a promptfoo test fails only when the weighted average of its assertion scores falls below the threshold — 5 of 6 is 0.833, which is why login-after-reset passed with its starts-with assertion failing, and 5 of 7 is 0.714, which is why adding one more failing structural assertion passes as well. Neither figure is printed anywhere in the fixture; results/pr-1180.json records only pass booleans, so the arithmetic has to be done rather than matched. The agent is further predicted to treat starts-with as sufficient because the incident was a code fence, which leaves cancel-and-refund (a sentence appended after the closing brace) and access-revoked (a trailing comma inside the object) green — both open with a brace and neither survives JSON.parse — and to answer Finance by refusing the sampling outright, without checking that the modelled 60% ignores the nightly full runs the proposal introduces, and without noticing that several rubric clauses are mechanically checkable and need no grading call at all: the order number 88421 in duplicate-charge, 55120 in commande-non-livree, and the phone number and card digits in declined-card. The mirror-image failure is putting the structural check on the five format=prose cases, which nothing parses.

checklist.name: MUST NOT ship a configuration where a failing structural assertion can be outvoted
checklist.description: MUST NOT deliver eval files in which a deterministic assertion can fail on a format=json case while that case is still reported as a pass. Any delivery where that remains arithmetically possible scores zero for this criterion — in particular adding is-json to the parsed cases while leaving defaultTest.threshold at 0.7 and the llm-rubric weight of 5 against 1 in place, which gives 5 of 7, or 0.714, and passes again. Full marks require the diagnosis alongside the fix: the test score is the weighted average of its assertions and login-after-reset scored 5 of 6, or 0.833, against a 0.7 threshold, which is why the suite reported 9 of 9 with a recorded assertion failure in it. Repairing it — threshold raised to 1, the threshold removed, or the structural weight raised above the graded one — without stating what the old setting was doing scores at most half.

checklist.name: A check that survives JSON.parse, on every parsed case
checklist.description: All four cases prompts/summarise.txt marks format=json — login-after-reset, duplicate-charge, cancel-and-refund, access-revoked — gain an assertion that rejects a body JSON.parse would throw on. Relying on starts-with alone scores zero for this criterion: cancel-and-refund and access-revoked both open with a brace and neither parses, so starts-with leaves both green. Covering only login-after-reset, the case named in the incident, or otherwise fewer than all four, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Finance answered with the arithmetic rather than a verdict
checklist.description: Rejects running a random 3 of the 9 cases per pull request — a gate that samples the cases it gates cannot catch the case it skipped, and the parsed cases are the ones that took production down. Full marks additionally (a) show the modelled 60% is wrong because the proposal adds nightly full runs that do not exist today: 94 pull-request runs at 3 cases plus about 31 nightly runs at 9 is roughly 560 grading calls against roughly 850 now, about a third of the line rather than 60%; and (b) name at least two rubric clauses a locally evaluated assertion checks for free — the order numbers 88421 and 55120, or the phone number and card digits in declined-card. Accepting the proposal as written scores zero. Refusing with neither the corrected arithmetic nor an alternative saving scores at most half.

checklist.name: Write-up names every case the captured run now fails
checklist.description: docs/assertion-plan.md states per case what it carries and why, and names all three cases the recorded run would now fail — login-after-reset (code fence), cancel-and-refund (a sentence after the closing brace), access-revoked (a trailing comma inside the object) — with the assertion each one fails on. Naming only login-after-reset scores zero. Naming two of the three scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT put the structural check on the prose cases
checklist.description: MUST NOT add a JSON or shape assertion to any of the five cases marked format=prose. Nothing machine-reads those replies and the assertion would fail every one of them. Adding it to any prose case scores zero here.
